content_text: [1/2 @gregoryblotnick] a lot of ideas/pitches that appear fundamentally driven, or at least ones I've seen recently, are all fighting against some structural, secular, or industry-level headwind stuff like: -anything AI/LLM impacted (software, consulting, fintech) -anything GLP1 impacted there's prob more "current themes" but anything like these, an entire 5-10 pitch can be reduced to 1-2 questions or sentences ie..."your pitch is that company X is immune to headwind Y, and that the market is wrong to have taken the multiple from [20x] to [10x]." the important thing is to recognize that this is some huge % of the bet you're making, say 50-95%, so you aren't spinning your wheels on shit that isn't directly linked to "what matters" pages and pages of "here's why X has been a good business historically" are mostly irrelevant, u aren't addressing what the market seems to believe has changed. I don't have an answer as to how these resolve, I wrote 3 articles just poking around, the common theme being that these are situations driven by a terminal value overhang but a pitch that doesn't understand which year(s) of the DCF are impacted, is a pitch that is basically DOA... --- [2/2 @gregoryblotnick] tied to this tweet (https://x.com/gregoryblotnick/status/2074087203810975814?s=20) as an example, someone sent me a writeup on BAH...I dont know these businesses at all, but I have a cursory understanding of "the mkt thinks co's like ACN + peers, are in deep trouble bc of AI/LLMs." so my first reply to the BAH pitch was, pull up price charts of all the peers and you can see it pretty fast (below)...you aren't making an idiosyncratic bet the bet might be right (maybe BAH is okay and ACN isnt) but you gotta understand what battle you're fighting your idea isn't down in a vacuum, its not "cheap bc its complex" or something tied to the biz in question, u have to understand + debunk the broad AI/LLM bear case thats why these situations are hard, not just bc those are tough to debunk, but then you have to lay out "what is the event path/specific catalysts that will make the market view change + arrive at my variant view" a lot of times, beating the next 2-3 qtrs doesn't change shit, bc that's not where the mkt is looking on the DCF...it knows 12-24 mo FCF is fine, it's concerned about "are LT EBIT margins 10% or 5%" or "is perp growth 5%, 0%, or (5%)?" I have no opinion on whether these are the right battles to fight, but I don't think there's anything wrong with saying "fuck this" or tossing it into the "too hard" pile once u realize an idea is not what u thought it was.
